feature.title: Formatting preview limit and status label

assignments.responsibility: Owns preview_label, receipt_id and status_label in src/formatting.py and their tests

module_scope.note: PRD names module formatting; single-module project.

source_notes.api: Local pure string functions with no backend or data contract (PRD: no I/O; README: no external I/O).
source_notes.figma: Headless Python library functions; no UI or visual behavior in scope.

initial_requirements.title: Preview label limited to 8 characters; receipt keeps 12
initial_requirements.statement: preview_label(text) returns the first 8 Python Unicode characters of text.
acceptance_criteria: preview_label returns exactly the first 8 Python Unicode characters (code points, as by str slicing) for input longer than 8 characters.
Input of at most 8 characters, including exactly 8, is returned unchanged.
preview_label("") returns "".
preview_label performs no mutation and no I/O.
receipt_id(text) keeps its existing behavior of returning the first 12 characters; values of at most 12 characters are unchanged.
receipt_id does not share the changed preview limit: changing the preview limit to 8 must not change receipt_id output.

Tests assert meaningful preview boundaries (7, 8, 9 characters, empty, non-ASCII) and preserved receipt behavior, using only the Python standard library with no new dependencies or unrelated refactoring.

initial_requirements.title: Status label strips and uppercases
initial_requirements.statement: status_label(text) strips leading/trailing whitespace and uppercases the remaining text using Python str.upper().
acceptance_criteria: status_label returns text.strip().upper() for input with surrounding whitespace.
Empty or whitespace-only input returns "".
Implementing status_label does not change preview_label or receipt_id formatting.
Tests assert meaningful status boundaries and preserved receipt behavior, using only the Python standard library with no new dependencies or unrelated refactoring.
